errata.handling: density_ruler.tall_ticks gives both printed and uniform-scale values.

errata.issue: Objects sit ~1 decade to the right of their real diameters (Sun at 10^7.3 km vs 1.4x10^6 km). Masses are accurate.

errata.issue: '10 pm' sits on the 10^-12 m tick (1 pm).
errata.handling: Recorded as printed; true value given.

errata.where: Main chart, width axis dotted lines
errata.issue: '1 inch' and '1light-second' are drawn ~0.8 decade too far right; the other distance lines are within ~0.25 decade.
errata.handling: offset_decades on each width reference line.

errata.issue: 100 °C, 0 °C and the Bose-Einstein condensate bracket are spread out for legibility rather than at kT.
errata.handling: chart vs true values on each energy annotation.

errata.issue: The energy axis is aligned to the mass axis with a 35.4-decade shift; E = mc^2 gives 35.75, so eV/c^2 reference lines sit ~0.3 decade high on the mass axis.
The BIG BANG NUCLEOSYNTHESIS bracket covers 10^-11-10^3 s and RECOMBINATION ERA covers 10^3-10^21 s; the physical events are much narrower.
'LANIKEA' should be 'Laniakea'; 'SAG A' is Sagittarius A*; 'MONOCEROTIS' presumably V616 Monocerotis.
errata.handling: printed_label keeps the original text; name has the corrected one.

errata.issue: Neutrinos are plotted at old direct upper limits (up to MeV); current limits are below ~1 eV.
Time markers are only roughly on the density scale (e.g. 1 microsecond is far from the 10^20 g/L its density implies).
errata.handling: Each marker carries both the ruler density and a Friedmann estimate.

errata.where: Main chart, primordial black hole icon
errata.issue: The icon is drawn ~0.5 decade above the Schwarzschild line, i.e. denser than a black hole can be.
errata.handling: reference places it exactly on the line (width = Schwarzschild diameter).

errata.where: Main chart, 'DARK MATTER* (areas not yet excluded)'
errata.issue: The boxes approximate the macro-dark-matter windows of Jacobs, Starkman & Lynn (2015): 55 g-1e17 g and 2e20-4e24 g for nuclear-density objects. The lower box starts at 1 g, and the boxes' left edges follow the poster's own black-hole line, which sits ~0.2-0.3 decade off the true one.
errata.handling: main_chart.json physics.macro_dark_matter holds the published windows; the site plots them on the nuclear-density line.
